questions.history: List the asset JAR by its absolute native path, using test paths containing no spaces. The asset exists only in that dependency.
questions.prediction: Parent is expected to miss the asset in a root-wildcard scan. The merge should return one matching resource whose bytes decode to amber.
questions.basis: The manifest names the JAR, and the known archive entry and bytes identify the required result independently of the resolver.
questions.refutation: The merge finds no match, reports two copies, or returns different contents.

questions.history: Put the dependency under lib beside the launcher and use the relative manifest entry lib/asset.jar.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should return the unique amber resource.
questions.basis: The pre-existing java -jar relative-path fixture exercises this supported layout.
questions.refutation: The resolver misses or duplicates this conventional manifest entry, or its stream yields different bytes.

questions.history: Hold the absolute path in the manifest fixed. In a separate fresh deployment replace the dependency with one whose same entry contains cobalt. Keep another same-named JAR containing amber outside the runtime class path.
questions.prediction: On the merge both launches should find one resource. Readback should change from amber to cobalt even though the matched resource filename is unchanged.
questions.basis: Only the declared dependency changed. Its known bytes distinguish the intended archive from a same-named decoy or the wrong resource root.
questions.refutation: The reported URL ends with the expected archive suffix but the data still reads amber, both versions of the resource appear, or the second scan is empty.
